title: When Not to Write Memory: Governing False Promotion from Correlated Agent Traces
title_zh: 何时不应写入记忆：从相关智能体轨迹中治理错误提升
abstract_en: Long-lived language agents increasingly write reusable memories from their own execution traces. The key safety question is not only what agents should remember, but when they should refuse to write memory at all. Repeated observations across agents are not necessarily independent evidence: the same claim may be copied from a shared source, induced by a shared prompt, stale under a new environment, or valid only in a narrower scope. We study this failure mode as a memory writepath governance problem. We introduce GovMem as a conservative diagnostic reference policy that estimates dependency-aware support, retrieves counterevidence, assigns scope, and outputs one of three decisions: promote, reject, or needs-review. In controlled synthetic stress tests, GovMem reduces false promotion from 0.597 to 0.040 in the default setting while preserving 0.960 recall, at an explicit review burden. In a project-internal 120candidate human-labeled real-trace subset spanning 79 recorded traces and project reports, dependency-aware promotion reduces false promotion from 0.371 for source+scope to 0.032 overall, but held-out false promotion remains 0.111 and the method is highly conservative, with 0.692 review burden and 0.448 direct recall. A final human adjudication of 133 high-impact external codingagent candidates is more severe: none are safe for automatic promotion, and all 11 verification-gate positives are rejected as boilerplate, shared-tool artifacts, file dumps, or non-reusable debugging traces. These results support GovMem primarily as a diagnostic governance design point, not as a generally validated or efficient automatic memory writer: agent memory write paths should be evaluated as risk-controlled evidence-governance systems, while broader external coverage and downstream harm evidence are still needed before stronger claims.
abstract_zh: 长期运行的语言智能体越来越多地从自身执行轨迹中写入可复用记忆。本文关注的安全问题不仅是智能体应该记住什么，更是何时应拒绝写入记忆。跨智能体的重复观察并不一定构成独立证据：同一声明可能来自共享来源、由相同提示诱导、在新环境中过时，或仅在更窄范围内成立。作者将该问题建模为记忆写入路径治理问题，并提出 GovMem：一种保守的诊断性参考策略，用于估计依赖感知的证据支持、检索反证、分配适用范围，并输出 promote、reject 或 needs-review 三类决策。在受控合成压力测试中，GovMem 在默认设置下将错误提升率从 0.597 降至 0.040，同时保持 0.960 的召回率，但带来显式人工审查负担。在项目内部 120 个候选、人工标注的真实轨迹子集上，覆盖 79 条记录轨迹和项目报告，依赖感知提升将 source+scope 基线的错误提升率从 0.371 降至整体 0.032；但留出集错误提升仍为 0.111，且方法高度保守，审查负担为 0.692，直接召回率为 0.448。最后对 133 个高影响外部 coding-agent 候选的人工裁决更为严苛：没有任何候选适合自动提升，11 个通过验证门的正例也均因样板文本、共享工具产物、文件转储或不可复用调试轨迹而被拒绝。结果表明，GovMem 更适合作为诊断性治理设计点，而非已普遍验证且高效的自动记忆写入器；智能体记忆写入路径应被评估为风险受控的证据治理系统，同时仍需更广泛的外部覆盖和下游危害证据支持更强结论。
key_points_zh: 论文指出，多智能体轨迹中的重复声明常受共享来源、共享提示、环境变化或作用域限制影响，不能简单视为独立证据并写入长期记忆。
提出 GovMem 作为保守诊断策略，包含依赖感知支持估计、反证检索、作用域分配，并给出 promote、reject、needs-review 三类写入决策。
在合成压力测试中，GovMem 将错误提升率从 0.597 降至 0.040，同时保持 0.960 召回率，但需要承担额外人工审查成本。
在项目内部真实轨迹子集上，依赖感知机制显著降低错误提升，但方法仍非常保守：审查负担高、直接召回低，留出集仍有错误提升。
外部 coding-agent 候选的人审结果显示无一适合自动提升，强调 GovMem 更像风险治理诊断框架，而非可直接部署的通用自动记忆写入器。

llm_assessment.comment: GovMem squarely targets memory write-path quality by treating promotion as dependency-aware evidence governance, though it remains conservative and diagnostic.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: GovMem 明确针对记忆写入质量，将记忆提升建模为依赖感知的证据治理问题，但目前更偏保守诊断用途。
